title: Modern JavaScript Essentials: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on the modern JS syntax and built-ins most used day to day: destructuring, spread/rest, safe access operators, template literals, array methods, ES modules, and Map/Set.

chapters.title: Modern JS Mental Model
points: Destructuring unpacks arrays by position and objects by key: const [a, b] = arr; const { x, y } = obj;
Spread (...) expands an iterable or object into elements; rest (...) collects the remaining items into one array or object. Same syntax, opposite direction
Optional chaining ?. short-circuits to undefined when the left side is null or undefined, instead of throwing a TypeError
Nullish coalescing ?? returns the right side only when the left is null or undefined
Template literals use backticks: `Hi ${name}` embeds any expression and allows multi-line strings

chapters.title: Destructuring, Spread and Rest in Practice
points: Rename and default in objects: const { id: userId, role = 'guest' } = user; defaults apply only when the value is undefined
Nested destructuring: const { address: { city } } = user; throws if address is undefined
Swap variables without a temp: [a, b] = [b, a]
Rest must come last: const [first, ...others] = arr; const { a, ...remaining } = obj
Spread makes a shallow copy and merges: const copy = { ...obj, k: 1 }; later keys override earlier ones; arrays: [...a, ...b]

chapters.title: Optional Chaining, ?? and Template Literals
points: Three forms of optional chaining: obj?.prop, obj?.[key], fn?.(args)
?? vs ||: || replaces every falsy value (0, '', false), ?? replaces only null and undefined; so count ?? 10 keeps 0
Optional chaining on a missing chain returns undefined, and it only guards the part immediately left of ?.; a?.b.c still throws if b is undefined
?? cannot be mixed with || or && without parentheses (SyntaxError); ??= assigns only if the current value is null or undefined

Tagged templates call a function with the string parts and values: tag`a${x}b`; in an untagged template, ${} values are converted to strings, so plain objects print [object Object]; a tag function receives the raw values

chapters.title: Array Methods: map, filter, reduce
points: map returns a new array of the same length by transforming each item; filter returns a new array of items whose callback is truthy
reduce((acc, item) => next, initial) folds an array into one value; always pass the initial value, since an empty array with no initial throws a TypeError
Callback forms: map((item, index, array)); and the parseInt gotcha: ['1','2','3'].map(parseInt) gives [1, NaN, NaN] because index is passed as the radix
Chaining example: orders.filter(o => o.paid).map(o => o.total).reduce((s, t) => s + t, 0)
map, filter and reduce do not mutate the original; sort, push, splice and reverse do mutate. Do not use map just for side effects, use forEach; in reduce, always return the accumulator

chapters.title: ES Modules and Map and Set
points: Named exports need exact names in braces: export const f = ...; import { f } from './m.js'; a default export is imported with any name: import f from './m.js'; and a module can have only one default export
Imports are live read-only bindings, not copies; modules run once and are cached, and they are strict mode by default
Dynamic import returns a promise: const m = await import('./m.js'); static imports must be at the top level; in Node, use .mjs or "type": "module", and include the file extension
Map holds key-value pairs with any type of key and keeps insertion order: set, get, has, delete, size; plain objects coerce keys to strings
Set stores unique values: new Set(arr) removes duplicates, [...new Set(arr)] gets the array back; Set and Map compare with SameValueZero, so NaN equals NaN but two {} objects are different

chapters.title: Modern JS Cheat Sheet
points: Destructure: const { a, b = 1, ...rest } = obj; const [x, , z] = arr
Spread/merge: {...a, ...b}, [...a, ...b], fn(...args)
Safe access: user?.address?.city ?? 'N/A'
Array pipeline: arr.filter(f).map(m).reduce(r, init)
Module syntax: export default x; export { y }; import x, { y } from './m.js'
Collections: new Map([[k, v]]), map.get(k), new Set(arr), set.has(v), [...set]
